scope: Pinned Windows allocation-hook runtime/thread and outer-lock source review; not universal native exclusion proof

task_contract.scope: Independent read-only Windows hook allocation exclusion and outer-lock investigation. Own scratch source/report artifacts only. No maintained edits, native probes, builds, remote dispatches, dependency changes or integration.

producer_report.result: Steady-state agent/linked-GLib thread exclusion is supported by exact source plus retained native progress. An unconditional claim that no runtime/control thread can enter the listener is unsupported: Windows/CRT/DLL startup before GLib realization lies outside its ignore extent. This is not a perfect allocation-provenance classifier, nor evidence of a newly executed compiler failure or universal deadlock.

established_protections.fact: Gum sets a per-thread callback guard before native onEnter/onLeave dispatch. Nested allocator calls made during our callbacks, including original retries and synchronization, bypass listeners. The guard is cleared before the initial original allocator body executes, so this is callback-extent recursion protection, not an outer allocator/caller lock guarantee.

Default native Interceptor.attach listeners honor the current thread ignore level. C callback pointers dispatch directly, without entering the JS scope/mutex. This resource uses native CModule callbacks, not JS allocation callbacks or replacements.
The injected agent explicitly establishes ThreadIgnoreScope(FRIDA_THREAD) around its run loop. ThreadIgnoreScope obtains the same interceptor and increments current-thread ignore.

gum_init_embedded installs callbacks on Frida linked GLib; gum_on_thread_realize ignores each such worker before its thread body, and its dispose/finalize hooks manage teardown ignore. The JS loop and script worker scheduler use this linked GLib thread machinery. This does not apply automatically to an application’s separately linked GLib or arbitrary CreateThread/OS callback threads.

Explicit NativeFunction traps:none increments ignore around ffi_call; it does not grant a global exclusion for every runtime operation. Cooperative default/traps:all calls may temporarily unignore an otherwise ignored thread. All production native control/query wrappers use traps:none.

Gum internal allocator and the Frida GLib memory vtable reduce use of the application Windows heap on their paths. Gum’s default non-diet Windows configuration selects internal dlmalloc mspaces backed by VirtualAlloc. These source branches are conditional; this review does not disassemble the exact native DLLs or claim every Windows/CRT call uses that allocator.

The Windows libc-shim branch initializes embedded Gum but does not define its own malloc/realloc replacements. Those replacements are in the non-Windows #else branch. Therefore the POSIX shim cannot establish Windows CRT allocator independence.

concrete_remaining_boundaries.status: Source-supported conditional counterexample, not an observed production failure
concrete_remaining_boundaries.minimal_case: A target DLL enables thread notifications. After hook installation a new Frida linked-GLib worker starts. The target DLL’s DLL_THREAD_ATTACH callback makes a positive flags0 RtlAllocateHeap request that actually returns NULL. This callback executes before GLib realization and is not protected by that later ignore call. The hook parks onLeave while this caller still owns loader lock.

windows_sources.supports: DLL_THREAD_ATTACH runs in the new thread; DllMain runs under process loader lock.
Microsoft explicitly documents allocating per-thread memory in thread-attach callbacks.

limits: Current actual compiler DLLs and the production post-install runtime thread-creation path have not been established here.
The already-running JS controller may still publish/grant and recover; retaining loader lock does not by itself prove all control operations deadlock.
Do not silently exempt all DLL/TLS/CRT paths or narrow required compiler coverage.

Thread origin and allocation ownership differ: a target DLL callback executing on a new Frida thread is still application code. Exempting the entire bootstrap thread would skip that application allocation and requires a coverage decision; no such exemption is selected.

concrete_remaining_boundaries.status: Inherent caller-state boundary; actual compiler incidence unknown
concrete_remaining_boundaries.minimal_case: An application calls HeapLock(H), then a supported real Rtl allocation on H returns NULL. Our onLeave waits before the caller can reach HeapUnlock(H). Other threads needing H cannot allocate or free. An application mutex around an allocation has the analogous dependency. Returning from the inner allocator does not release such caller-owned locks.

windows_sources.supports: Only the owning thread can allocate/free until HeapUnlock; other heap users block.

limits: Artificial commit-limit restoration by an external controller can still make the retained thread progress.
The source cannot establish that granting or freeing unrelated work always resolves the same-process memory dependency.

The user-authorized whole-task terminate/retry fallback is the appropriate existing recovery boundary when retained memory/locks prevent progress; implementation belongs to WindowsAttempt/controller owners.

concrete_remaining_boundaries.status: Unresolved Windows private call graph, not a confirmed defect
concrete_remaining_boundaries.minimal_case: If RtlReAllocateHeap internally invokes hooked RtlAllocateHeap while retaining a heap-internal lock, an inner allocation onLeave can park while the outer allocator remains active. Gum clears its callback guard during the original allocator body. Existing wait frames identify bytes/thread/error but not which allocator callback produced the wait.
limits: No claim that the retained Windows builds take this nested path.
No claim that private Windows heap locks remain held merely because a returned allocation failed.
Avoid replacing this unknown with an unsupported universal claim that onLeave means every allocator lock has been released.

producer_report.production_readiness_conclusion: Keep the accepted primitive native gate and proceed with separately owned production composition. Do not advertise universal runtime allocator exclusion or universal lock-free parking. Any failure involving a pre-realize/outer-lock context must retain provenance and use an external whole-owned-workload recovery boundary. No dependency workaround or coverage reduction is selected.
